reason: The reflector petals need a supporting structure, so this seems like a direct start on the solar furnace.
expectation: I expect a supported reflector assembly, though it may still need the receiver and tracking drive.

alternatives.reason: The mesh may help prepare the regolith feedstock, but I want to start with the furnace.

effect: The supported reflector is ready for the receiver, so I can continue building the furnace.
reaction: The result matched my expectation, though it gave no further detail.
reason: Adding the receiver seems like the next direct step toward a working solar furnace.
expectation: I expect a furnace assembly that concentrates sunlight onto the receiver, possibly still needing the tracking drive.

alternatives.reason: Preparing a screen could advance the feedstock goal, but I prefer to continue the furnace first.

effect: The furnace is complete and operating; the remaining goal is to prepare feedstock.
reaction: The focused sunlight heating the receiver is a clear, satisfying result.
reason: This is the only offered combination and likely makes a screen for the regolith.
expectation: I expect a framed screen for separating the excavated material, though its exact role is uncertain.

effect: The sieve is ready to sort the excavated regolith for feedstock.
reaction: The result was straightforward and matched my expectation.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should prepare the material for forming.
expectation: I expect the sieve to separate finer regolith from larger fragments.

effect: The regolith is now screened to an even size and ready for forming.
reaction: The separation of coarse stones makes the preparation step clear.
reason: The press is the only offered action and should form the screened material.
expectation: I expect the press to compact the regolith into a formed feedstock, though I don't know its final shape.

effect: The feedstock goal is complete; the blanks have shape but still need firing for strength.
reaction: The distinction between compaction and firing was a useful, physically sensible detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Pressing the screened regolith was most worthwhile: the explanation made clear why the weak blanks need support until firing.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the supported reflector was the least engaging moment: the result confirmed the expected assembly without adding detail.

surprise.text: I was interested that pressing gives the blanks shape but not finished strength; firing must bond their grains.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the sieve and press were the only offered combinations at their respective steps.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the solar furnace fires the blanks and what the material becomes; the process so far has been clear but fairly guided.
